reason: This passage from Exodus 3 centers on God's covenant with the patriarchs and His concern for the suffering Israelite people in Egypt. God's motivation expressed here is hearing the cry of His people (צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) and witnessing their oppression (הַלַּחַץ אֲשֶׁר מִצְרַיִם לֹחֲצִים אֹתָם). While the passage mentions that the Israelites will serve God on 'this mountain' (הַהָר הַזֶּה), the thematic emphasis is clearly on God's relationship with His people and His redemptive action, not on the intrinsic importance of land to Him. The statement conflates territorial concern with the actual focus of the text, which is God's care for His covenant people and their liberation.
